name: PineCount – Analytics, Page Views, Live Visitors, AdSense
author: Ritesh

sections.description:
PineCount records pageviews in your site’s own database and shows them in a clean dashboard inside wp-admin. Nothing is sent to a third-party analytics service.

It works with full-page caching: a small script reports each pageview from the browser, so cached pages are counted too.

What you get

  • Pageviews, visitors, sessions and views per visit, by hour, day, week or month.
  • Engaged time: how long each page and each visit was actually in use, not just open.
  • Top pages, entry pages, referrers, traffic sources, devices and on-site searches.
  • Filters: click any page, referrer, source, device, search or outbound link to see the whole dashboard for just that, and combine as many as you like.
  • Outbound links: which links to other sites your visitors click.
  • Choose which dashboard cards to show, and drag them into your own order.
  • Comparison with the previous period.
  • A dashboard widget and an admin bar counter for today’s numbers.
  • Optional live visitors, using any Redis server: on your own host or a hosted one. No PHP extension needed.
  • Optional Google AdSense earnings, page views, RPM and CTR next to your traffic.
  • A read-only REST API, protected by a key you generate, for pulling reports into other tools.
  • Data retention from 30 days to 5 years, and excluded paths with wildcards.

Privacy

  • No cookies and no persistent visitor ID. A visitor is identified only by a hash of their IP address and browser, mixed with a secret salt that changes every day, so nobody can be followed from one day to the next. The IP address itself is never stored.
  • Sessions use the browser’s per-tab session storage, which is cleared when the tab closes.
  • Engaged time is a number of seconds per pageview, counted in the browser while the page is on screen and in use. Nothing about what was done on the page is recorded.
  • Outbound links are stored as the site and page clicked to, never their query string.
  • Logged-in users are not tracked unless you turn that on.
  • You can honour the browser’s Do Not Track signal from the settings.
  • All data stays in your WordPress database.

External services

This plugin connects to outside services only if you set them up in its settings: Google, if you connect Google AdSense, and a Redis server, if you add one for live visitors. Until you do, it makes no external requests.

Redis server for live visitors (the address you enter) is used to keep the last few minutes of pageviews for the live visitors count.

  • Nothing is sent until you save a Redis URL in Analytics → Settings → Live visitors.
  • After that, each pageview’s page path, referring site, source, device type, on-site search term and the daily-changing visitor hash are sent to that server. They expire there after about four minutes. No IP address is sent.
  • If the URL points at a hosted Redis service, that service’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

Google OAuth (accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com) is used to authorise read-only access to your AdSense account.

  • When you click “Connect with Google”, your browser goes to Google’s sign-in page with your OAuth client ID.
  • After you approve, the plugin sends your OAuth client ID, client secret and the authorisation code to Google to get a refresh token. The token is stored encrypted in your database.
  • Before each report request, the plugin sends the client ID, client secret and refresh token to get a short-lived access token.
  • When you click “Disconnect”, the refresh token is sent to Google to be revoked.

Google AdSense Management API (adsense.googleapis.com) is used to read your earnings.

  • While connected, the plugin requests today’s estimated earnings, page views and clicks for your site every 10 minutes, and the last 7 days once a day, so Google’s later corrections are picked up.
  • It also lists your AdSense accounts and sites once when you connect, to find the site that matches this website.
  • Only your access token and the account and site IDs are sent. No visitor data is ever sent to Google.

Google’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Google APIs Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the Plugins screen, or upload the pinecount folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. Tracking starts straight away.
  3. Open Analytics in the admin menu to see your dashboard, and Analytics → Settings to adjust tracking, retention and the optional features.

Live visitors (optional)

Live visitors need a Redis server, either on your own host or a hosted one such as Upstash or Redis Cloud. No PHP extension or wp-config.php change is needed.

  1. Go to Analytics → Settings → Live visitors.
  2. Paste the server’s URL, such as redis://127.0.0.1:6379 or rediss://default:password@host:port for a TLS connection, switch live visitors on and save.
  3. Click Check connection to make sure it works.

Google AdSense (optional)

  1. In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client of type “Web application” and enable the AdSense Management API.
  2. Add the redirect URI shown in Analytics → Settings → AdSense to that client.
  3. Paste the client ID and secret into the settings, save, and click Connect with Google.
sections.faq:
Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Pageviews are reported from the browser, so pages served from a cache are still counted.

Does it use cookies?

No. See the Privacy section above.

Where is the data stored?

In seven tables in your WordPress database, prefixed pinecount_. You choose how long raw pageviews and outbound clicks are kept.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

By default, deleting the plugin removes its tables and settings. Turn off “Delete all data on uninstall” in the settings if you want to keep them.

Is there an API?

Yes. Generate a key in the settings, then send it in the X-PineCount-Key header. The full reference is under Analytics → Settings → API.
sections.changelog:
1.5.0

  • New: Engaged time. PineCount measures how long each page was actually in use: on screen, and used within the last 30 seconds. A tab in the background or left open while its reader is away stops counting.
  • New: Visit duration on the dashboard, the average engaged time of a visit. It follows filters and the comparison with the previous period.
  • New: Time on page in the full Top pages table, the average engaged time of a view of each page.
  • Changed: Bounce rate is removed, from the dashboard and the API. Engaged time says more about whether a page was read.
  • API: /report returns visit_duration and compare.visit_duration, and pages in /report and /pages return time_on_page, in place of the bounce_rate fields.
  • Note: Engaged time is measured from this version on. Earlier periods show a dash.

1.4.0

  • New: Filters. Click anywhere on a row in Top pages, Entry pages, Referrers, Traffic sources, Devices, Site searches or Outbound links to see the whole dashboard for just that: the chart, the figures, the comparison, every card and View all. Combine as many as you like, and remove them from the chips above the chart. Filtered views can be bookmarked.
  • New: Referrers, Traffic sources and Devices show visitors beside views, and every card shows both whatever the chart is showing.
  • New: The API’s /report and /pages accept the same filters (f_page, f_referrer, f_source and more) and say which were applied. Referrers, sources and devices in /report include visitors.
  • Changed: AdSense figures are hidden while the dashboard is filtered, and null in a filtered API report, since AdSense only covers the whole site.

1.3.0

  • New: Live visitors connect to Redis through a URL in Analytics → Settings → Live visitors, such as redis://127.0.0.1:6379, or rediss://user:password@host:port for a hosted server over TLS.
  • New: The Redis URL is stored encrypted and shown hidden, with an eye button to reveal it.
  • Changed: Live visitors no longer need the PhpRedis extension or the WP_REDIS_* settings in wp-config.php, and work with any Redis or Valkey version, not only 7.4 and later.
  • Changed: Live visitors are kept separately for each site, so one Redis server can be shared by several sites.

1.2.0

  • New: Outbound links. Clicks on links to other sites are counted, by site and page, and shown in a new dashboard card. Only the site and page are stored, never the query string.
  • New: Customize menu on the dashboard, to choose which cards are shown. Each user’s choice is kept for them.
  • New: Dashboard cards can be dragged into any order, or moved with the arrow keys. Each user’s order is kept for them.
  • New: /report includes outbound_links, the most clicked links for the period.
  • Changed: The Site searches card is hidden by default. Switch it back on from Customize.
  • Tweak: Data retention removes old outbound clicks along with old pageviews.

1.1.0

  • New: API endpoint /live, the number of visitors on the site right now.
  • New: API endpoint /live/report, live visitors by page, entry page, referrer, source, device and search, all from one reading.
  • New: /summary accepts compare=true, adding the previous period’s figures and the change on each.
  • Changed: /summary and /report no longer include live_users; request /live instead. /summary returns adsense_page_views in place of page_rpm, which /report still provides.
  • Fix: The dashboard widget’s axis numbers are no longer partly hidden at 10,000 views and above.
  • Tweak: Clearer API documentation on currency, sessions, bounce rate and date handling.

1.0.2

  • Renamed to PineCount.
  • New: Settings link on the Plugins screen.
  • New: Check connection button in the Live visitors settings, to test the Redis server.
  • Tweak: The live visitors requirements notice is hidden once live visitors are switched on.
  • Tweak: The API key header is now X-PineCount-Key.
  • Tweak: The Analytics menu now sits below the core WordPress menus.
  • Tweak: Stricter escaping of icons and the API documentation page, and stricter sanitizing of settings.

1.0.1

  • Fix: Saving the settings page now works.
  • Tweak: All admin and widget styles, IDs and data attributes now use the unique pinecount prefix, to avoid clashes with other plugins.
  • Tweak: Removed leftover code for moving data from an earlier development version.

1.0.0

  • First public release.

short_description: Lightweight, self-hosted analytics. Pageviews, visitors and traffic sources, stored in your own database with no cookies.

upgrade_notice.1.5.0: Replaces bounce rate with engaged time: Visit duration and Time on page. API clients: bounce_rate is gone; read visit_duration and time_on_page instead. The update adds two columns to the pageviews table, which can take a moment on a large site.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Adds filters: click any row on the dashboard to see everything for just that page, referrer, source or device. The API's /report and /pages accept the same filters.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: Live visitors now use a Redis URL set in the plugin's settings instead of the WP_REDIS_* settings in wp-config.php. If live visitors were on, add your Redis URL under Analytics → Settings → Live visitors to turn them back on.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Adds outbound link tracking and a dashboard you can customize and reorder. The Site searches card is now hidden by default; switch it back on from Customize.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: API change: /summary and /report no longer return live_users (use the new /live endpoint), and /summary returns adsense_page_views instead of page_rpm. The dashboard is unaffected.
